name: fast-project-start
body:
`apg project start` is near-instant when the main checkout's scan is current for main's HEAD. After the unchanged refusals (in-worktree, unborn/detached main, version gate, dirty main), start checks whether the main checkout's scan is fresh for main's HEAD (`git::is_fresh` over the main layout root) — the guard is `!is_fresh`, because `git::is_stale` alone returns false for an absent `db.lbug`/`graph.jsonl`, so it detects a missing scan only through `!is_fresh`. For a stale or missing scan, start REFUSES with guidance to run `apg scan` in the main checkout first. For a fresh scan, start creates the branch + worktree (off the default branch, unchanged) and copies the main checkout's `apg/.trans` artifacts into the new worktree's `apg/.trans`, with zero scan and zero frontend spawns. This is correct with zero re-assembly because the graph stores repo-relative paths (`path`/File FQN are repo-relative, rather than worktree-absolute), so main's DB is valid verbatim in the worktree; the worktree's tree equals main's HEAD, so the recorded content identity still matches.

Acceptance criteria:
- Starting a project when main's scan is stale or missing refuses, and the refusal tells the user to run `apg scan` in the main checkout.
- Starting a project when main's scan is fresh for main's HEAD spawns zero frontend processes.
- The resulting branch DB contains the same code nodes and edges as a full scan of main's HEAD under the same effective scan configuration (the blacklist stays outside the cache key, so a recorded config mismatch is undetectable from the store — see the cache-key note).
- The copy completes with zero full-tree walk of the source files.
- Correctness is preserved because main's scan is valid verbatim in the new worktree (repo-relative paths; the worktree's tree equals main's HEAD).
